Daily Lexapro for detail. Not totally sure if this is the right space for this. Someone tell me if I'm doing internet wrong - right now I'm looking for either insight or solidarity. Solidarity doesn't have to be "your experience matches mine," just, "hey, I've also had experiences that were tangentially related!" which I'm sure some of you have.

Day 1 was fun in a manic way. Some involuntary muscle jerking and nausea but music sounded really good+meaningful and I felt way more present in my body and surroundings than usual so I was stoked. I usually get some cool energy like that when I take my medication at the wrong time so it wasn't surprising or new, though it's usually followed by variant ramifications over the next couple of days.

What followed was feeling real weird and sensitive. Straight up cried about my sense of mental isolation and alienation because I made a crappy joke about -- wait for it -- Franz Ferdinand, and my girlfriend tried to communicate with me positively about how to have made a joke that was more easy to follow back and forth. I am really, really not a crier. I keep my shit locked in good and let it eat me alive without messing with my sense of self or others' perceptions so that was a weird thing.

Day 2: Woke up detached and foggy and unmotivated but still capable of going through the motions - not overwhelmed by obligation. After eating some breakfast and starting to feel like a person I got more of that feeling-more-present-in-my-self-and-surroundings thing but now I'm crying all over town! I was listening to a song on the bus by someone I knew in high school that I'm 90% sure alludes (in a compassionate and understanding way) to a friend of ours committing suicide three years ago. So, then, I was crying on the bus. It didn't feel terrible - if anything it felt cathartic and important - but again, I'm not a crier and definitely not publicly. If I show any emotion in public I figure that everyone around me deeply, deeply resents me for whatever privilege they assume I have the same way that I resent my customers who clearly make too much money and have entitled hissy fits. Because it sort of feels relieving and... legitimate (I don't want to keep using the word "important" or say "this is so REAL, man!") I am wondering if it signifies not only the chemical imbalance of being out of my meds but the emotional ramifications of all of the things I don't really have space or give myself space to deal with. When I get too-too drunk I get emotional about all of my dead friends and whoever is near me has to listen to me because I'm drunk and don't know what boundaries are, but other times there just isn't really an avenue to talk about it particularly since I don't have anyone else who was a mutual friend around me in real life to be like "oh yeah, that's still weird for me too." Sense of isolation is a different thing that I mostly don't care about. I'm weird and I can be alienating but most of the time I pull it off in a way that I can tell is very charming with people who I'm not terribly interested in getting to know anyway. (Customer service problems and generalized life problems with having highly specified interests and an abnormal pattern of socialization, really.)

I'm not really sure I still want to be medicated because it feels kind of good to have all of these person-feeling but I know that I also get ragingly suicidal at least monthly un-medicated and that without medication I've never, ever made it through a semester before without having a breakdown, getting ashamed about not showing up, and then not showing up. I also sort of feel like my subconscious just wants me to stop taking medication so that I can do empatheogenic drugs if I feel like it and not be nervous about interactions with psychedelics. (CAN YOU TELL THAT I'M ALL OVER THE PLACE?)

I appreciate the sentiment that you're trying to encourage but our views on the matter at hand are different. I definitely believe that life is difficult for everybody and that I am (despite my username) not a fragile waif-like creature unprepared and unequipped for the big scary world. However, I also sincerely believe that mental illness is a chemical imbalance that is as worthy of medical attention/treatment as any other disease so on that front I disagree with you wholly. Personally, I've always powered through and clearly survived to keep trying but I don't feel like there's any extra valor to be found in powering through a neuroses-charged hard mode to achieve anything. Valor is found in achievements themselves, and I consider active and mindful self-care to be an achievement in itself including but not limited to treating neuroses with medication should the need arrive - the majority has to do with reflection and personal determination of what needs to be attended to for self-improvement and personal well-being. The best parallel I can use for describing my general state at this time is "in remission."

My experiences going between medications and getting off them have had somewhat similar oddities. I remember one particular day that I had run out of my medication (I think it was cymbalta at the time) and my day was wonky.

My emotions were all over the place, and my energy levels matched them. It was a Saturday and so I began my day like any weekend - on the Internet - but after a while I became almost pissed at myself for not being active on a regular basis. So I decided to go for a jog (keep in mind I hadn't ran for almost a year). I began running and about a quarter mile out I started yelling at myself (mostly inner yelling... Mostly) to run harder and faster because reasons. I then started to almost argue with that mood and try to reason through what my emotions were going through.

I eventually got back to my house and sat down by the mailbox and starting crying. I just felt so anxious and distressed (what about I'm still not sure) that I just started letting it out. Then after a while of sitting there I startied laughing thinking how ridiculous the whole situation was and how insane I must have looked. Suffice to say the rest of the day continued on in that pattern of random mood swings.

And don't get me started about being all over the place now that I've been off my medications for a good 6 months. I've learned to tune it back around other people, but my mind can still be a chaotic mess wrapped around a Gordian knot.

I am on lexapro as well... when I tried to stop/taper abut 3 weeks after I got severe (for me) anxiety I had my 2nd ever panic attack and I felt like hell every day/night I couldnt sleep I was a mess. I started taking my normal dose and I got back to normal in about 2-3 weeks... I do not know but withdrawl from these medications is a bitch!

I learned the basics of C, but now i feel that i have a powerful tool and i'm not using it. People say work on a project or participate in an open source project. I have tried that, but i feel that there are lots of things i don;t know about. People suggested to start working with open source projects and learn on the way, but when reading the documentations of a project i discover that i only know that there is a programming language called C, so how can i participate with them if i don't know what the flying fuck is going on. For example i tried working on the Linux kernel, but discovered that i need to learn about it, which is entirely a sea on it's own.

Could someone tell me what can i do with C ? Not just the usual answer of "anything", and do i need to learn anything else after the basics, or are there any projects that i can participate in without feeling stupid as shit.

I would say find something you are interested in and/or know a bit about and find a way to apply your new knowledge. I was in the same boat after learning a bit of Java. At the time I was working at a casino so I decided to make a little slot machine game. Allowed me to work with math functions, a bit of graphics, and really just coding in general. If all else fails, look up entry level programming assignments and try to complete them.

What I typically do is try to come up with a project that someone around me will find useful. Usually basic stuff like, I made a webapp for my kids that's basically an allowance bank account. So I'll put their allowance in there and then they can see their balance, withdraw, see what they spent it on, etc. I know that isn't what you'd be doing in C, but just an example.
If you like the idea of game development, the Uzebox is a hobbyist 8 bit console that you program in C due to the restrictions of the processor.
